The atmosphere in this game is so surreal and nostalgic at same time, the end of the world is coming, but you're a kid and you have other things to worry about. It's good, weird, atmospheric af and there's a lot of cats to pet.

This game was advertised as something akin to Outer Wilds and metroidbranias, that unfortunately is not all true. It technically is correct that you can learn about the game and there is a loop where everything resets, that "knowledge" is mostly item placements and character dialogue. Learning about the world comes in exposition that feels random, less like learning and more like being told that the developer decided this was a thing that is on the game that you didn't have access to beforehand. The game is also very unpolished, physics feel wonky sometimes, most common example of that was if you ran up the sets of stairs you'd always be launched up with momentum as if it was a ramp. The NPC interaction also could use tweaking, my main issue with that was when the game would decide that cats will follow you around and the interaction seems to be decided by which entity is the closest to you, so almost every time I wanted to interact with something I had to move so the cats wouldn't be as close to me as the other thing, or I'd pet it instead. I've heard people complaining about the camera but that wasn't an issue for me. There might be more to be said, likely about the game design and such, but I think this is enough to prove my point. From advertisement, I came here expecting a world I could explore and immerse myself into, where I would have choices of what to do. This is not the experience I was given and I'll be refunding it. (got it as a gift)

品不到什么作者性，只见到满溢而出的自我意识。 ---首先时间循环完全是噱头，[b]本作完全不是一个基于时间循环的探索向游戏[/b]，除了二十分钟单局时限和星际拓荒的设计语言没有一分钱关系。即使去掉这个时间系统九成以上的沙盒体验不会有任何改变。OW的二十一分钟足够让一个星系天地异变，但本作的二十分钟却只能让小街区燃起一堆火（是的没错 除了一堆定时点燃的篝火没有任何其他根据时间推进的元素）。 ---其次knowledge-based完全是噱头，[b]本作基本毫无合格的知识锁设计[/b][spoiler]（除非把“某某东西放在哪”这种程度信息也算作“知识锁”）[/spoiler]，游戏角色并不会意识到自己身处循环，也没有谜题基于层层递进的知识编排结构展开；所谓的“知识驱动”大概是指“蓝蚱蜢在高处黑蚱蜢在洞穴”“某人可以算命”“某处可以交换物品”[spoiler]（不是编的是游戏里真的有）[/spoiler]之类再基础不过的信息。而再搞笑不过的是几个结局的触发方式的引导是[b]直接问作者化身的NPC[/b]，手把手给你说A结局在哪触发B结局在哪触发，真给我看大脑升级了 -以上倒只是不自量力去碰瓷OW的bad advertising，而只作为nostalgia向的步行模拟也只能说是一般般，只有一些哈代拉居民楼和东欧社区游乐场算是花了心思的，比起dreamcore还差了三个千禧梦（值得一提的是有个算命npc会随机给主角各种buff，不同的buff和许多结局/事件关联，所以如果要收集全结局就得一遍又一遍地roll加成buff、、步行模拟加这种环节真的蛮搞笑的（） -视觉和文本都有ai参与 ---教导意味溢出。 本作中的世界毁灭是因为名为“黑浪”的滔天海啸降临，但游戏在在前十分钟就放弃任何世界观构建而但借npc之口说些“黑浪其实是时间的隐喻一切都会在黑浪下摧毁消逝”；流程中时不时作者化身就会蹦出来教教你关于与时间相处的人生小哲理。一会“虽然你的黑浪也许不会在二十分钟之内到来，但最终依然会到来，所以赶紧去生活吧！”一会又是“下个循环不要尝试去达成目标了，接受无聊吧，仅仅去感受时间是如何流逝的，去feel it——”、、、、、全篇除了这种对于时间的大焦虑再没有其他考量，真要说的话这些青年小学习还不如OW里加布罗和切特面对超新星爆炸的几段小对话有意味。 将时间焦虑置于末日前二十分钟实在是浅得不能再浅的一个切片，这也使得作品看似玄奥的选题下内里空洞浅薄。本作在ins上最火的一条宣传视频下最高赞的评论是“Average Palestinian child’s life btw”——说实话如果这款游戏真的是由加沙人做给自己国土的，那么这一切也许会有宝贵之处：人们过着朝不保夕的生活，承载一切记忆的街区在难以解释的黑幕之下沦为废墟，对悲惨命运的不解与身处历史缝隙的悲哀……可惜这些都不会在本作看到。真是个该死的玩笑，因为这款游戏是[b]以色列作者[/b]做的。 为什么要专门提这么一嘴？前天打完之后顺手翻了作者的社媒，这位作者在发售日前一天（3.2）用希伯来文发了这样一条动态： [quote][i]“明天晚上8点——我希望那时伊朗不会发射任何武器。但即便有，我也会发布游戏——演出必须继续。🌊[/i][b][i]😅[/i][/b][i]”[/i][/quote] 一字未改。就且不说以伊双方炸民用设施的事件量有多不对等了，仅仅两天之前（2.28）美以联合轰炸期间才炸了一所女子学校杀了180名学生教师，有脸说这话吗？明明已经是道德低洼了还恬不知耻地抖机灵，甚至我玩你的游戏的那天以就在轰炸黎的民用设施，看看自己做的游戏这种对比不显得荒诞吗？ 以色列游戏业基本被网赌菠菜充斥，而本作能在普遍圈米的业界另辟蹊径确有不易，然而当时对这个游戏抱有的桃源幻想，现在看来简直可笑。你甚至可以看到锡安分子在部分差评下问出“既然你恨以色列为什么要给玩这个游戏来送钱呢？” 哈，好吧，那这就是我写这篇红评的原因：[b]我不推荐任何人购买或游玩这个游戏。[/b]如果想要找OW代餐请直接掉头左转《色度零》《Amatsuko》，如果想要怀旧体验或阈限空间也大有佳作可选，加上ai使用以及九国语言机翻无中文，我实在想不到有什么玩这个游戏的必要。 [i]浪潮啊浪潮，请你跨过高楼和蚱蜢、跨过那些栏杆和预言，去淹没月亮、淹没假象——去淹没一切戏弄你的人吧。[/i]

Unfortunately this game doesn't feel finished at all. It feels incomplete and chaotic. The main theme of the game is the passage of time, which is an amazing theme that could be expanded in many different interesting ways. And through projecting through authors self-insert we are experiencing this theme in a neighborhood where Alex grew up. Since it was based on a neighborhood from Rishon LeTzion, a neighbor city to my hometown, I am very familiar with the setting and was excited mainly because of it. Unfortunately the visual and a pair of eastereggs the resemblence of the setting disappears. The game breaks the forth wall pretty often, the Hebrew localization(Which I assumed would be native to the game!) is incomplete. Some activities in the game are either pointless or have zero to no connection, closer to my 90% of completion I had to open a guide to see couple of last steps. The mechanical part of the game itself is very buddy, the movements, the mirror reflections, the fact that its very tempting to press E in Gorewar2099 but it just puts you in a very long and boring cutscene. Some supernatural things and the 4th wall breaking just look out of place and ruin the message the author attempted to convey. I wish the author will use this experience to keep developing games with better quality and polishing, maybe this project will allow his team to expand or to inspire other indie developers who will actually use our setting in their games. But currently - I would not reccomend buying this game UNLESS you are willing to support our local gamedev, AND want to see your neighborhood you grew up in, in a videogame. תודה אלכס!

The game was alright. The gameplay isn't anything revolutionary and neither is the story. I got most of the endings within the first couple hours, so there's no harm in buying the game, playing it for 2 hours, and refunding it. You can tell the game wants to have fun, puzzley secret endings, but it falls short of that by relying on characters to explicitly tell you how to get each ending. There is a good amount of AI art in the game so if you care about that, definitely don't play it. The story and writing was rather lazy; I didn't really care about much when playing the game. As I previously mentioned most (if not all) endings are directly spoonfed to the player through dialogue. The game is not afraid to straight up tell the player what they should feel about the game. At least 5 different NPCs literally tell you the primary theme of the game, word for word, and its not very interesting either. If you want a game that does this much better (sorry steam gods if im not allowed to say this) but Outer Wilds, which likely was a heavy inspiration for this game, does this concept a lot better and is a lot more fun. I'd give the game a solid 4/10, when you're in the rhythm of things then it can be slightly enjoyable, but I found the video game section to be a slog and the irl sections to be interesting, if only for a short amount of time. I'm still gonna say I don't recommend the game, primarily so this review is more visible, but, to be completely honest, buying the game, playing it for an hour, and refunding the game if you aren't enjoying it isn't a bad idea, Its 9$ whatever nobody cares really.

Eternal Afternoon is one of those games that won't click with everyone, but it definitely clicked with me. The story is told in a subtle, abstract way, and you really have to read between the lines to appreciate what it's trying to say. If you're expecting everything to be explained directly, you might not enjoy it. I personally loved piecing everything together. The atmosphere is fantastic. It's melancholic, a bit depressing, and somehow captures that distinct Eastern European vibe that makes everything feel nostalgic and strangely comforting at the same time. I played it in one sitting (actually, several playthroughs back to back). I read every single dialogue and genuinely enjoyed the writing and the characters. My only real complaint: what was the point of collecting all the kites? I gathered every single one and never got any reward or acknowledgment for it. That felt disappointing after putting in the extra effort. Even with that minor frustration, I had a great time. This game accomplishes what it sets out to do, and it left a lasting impression on me. If you enjoy narrative-driven games with an emotional atmosphere and don't mind connecting the dots yourself, I can definitely recommend Eternal Afternoon.

I was recommended this game from a friend and heard good things about it, bought the game and I've let it sit in my library for months(had the game downloaded and all, just didn't bother to play it or even open it). And one day, out of boredom decided to play the game and well.. WOW The game looked normal at first, but as I continued to play more and more and started collecting collectibles and really relating to the vibe of the game's world it really became something special to me, something I cared about, cared about it enough to finish the game entirely, and cared about it enough to come back to it back to back for 2 days straight. Not to mention the theme of the game which is that time flies, and there's nothing you can do to stop it so enjoy your life. Some of the people you meet have interesting dialog like [spoiler] Gabriel and his speech of life and death [/spoiler], or [spoiler] Sapir and her story and why she wants to end it all [/spoiler]. Also one character in particular I really liked is [spoiler] Mr.Llun [/spoiler] His dialog is most interesting and gives the vibes of a chill dude with a lot of knowledge([spoiler] Also the fact that he's like Alex Klexber the developer talking to the player instead of the protagonist) [/spoiler]. [spoiler] Another thing I liked is the many endings this game has [/spoiler] [spoiler] My favourite ending is definitely is the 6th ending where the player rides the wave and grows up. [/spoiler] [spoiler] First of all messing with the settings and finding a slider to get a surfboard? That's such a cool way to start the proccess of getting this ending. But when you actually get the ending and ride the wave and the cutscene plays out, it really left me speechless just seeing the character of Sasha all grown up, moving out of his appartement which is the only one that is old while all the other buildings are newer and higher buildings. It made me feel so related because i have friends who lived at old houses and they moved out because the city wanted that area for newer buildings, I have a newer building right in front of my kinda old house and just seeing the comparison bewtween them is too different world, yet, they still are in the same street. [/spoiler] Overall, I think this is the best walking simulator I've ever played, with little elements of horror, (but not in the way you feel the game is based around the genere cause it's really not). Good atmospheric soundtrack and a GREAT GAME which is definitely meant for you to explore all the way. The only criticism I can give is that there are so achievements that require some luck, And that I did needed to restart a lot and some achievements require you to do specific things, that restart your game, so you'd have to restart and do all the steps again, but not something that happens often. 9/10

This game is something truly unique. It captures a very specific moment in time — the vibe of Israeli housing projects in the ’90s — with almost eerie accuracy. And honestly, anyone who grew up in similar projects in Eastern Europe, the U.S., or the U.K. will instantly recognize the atmosphere. It’s wild how a computer game can mirror that reality so well. This one actually pulled me straight back into my childhood, in a way most modern games just don’t manage anymore

What a sweet sweet game. A calm walking simulator where you can walk around the neighborhood before the world ends. Or is it? So much stuff is packed in this little gem. Secrets for you to discover, people to talk to, little moments from the past. And from the future. This game can be a walking sim; a first person shooter, a platformer, a metrioidbrainia, an ars-poetic reflection of video games, or a nostalgic reflection of life itself; if you want it to be. The amount of things to discover in this little neighborhood is immense. I got hooked from the first play until I uncovered everything.

Well I've never played a game that looked so much like my childhood (and yes that complaint is directed both towards the lack of games that take place in the suburbs of the greater DC metropolitan area, as it is towards the lack of games set in suburban Israel). Also I'm glad I'm not the only person on the planet who hates texture filtering (may it burn in hell). What really caught my attention was just how easy it was to ignore the impending apocalypse, to treat our 20min peak into little Sasha's life as just another afternoon, not the last one, and just... do whatever. Play video-games, talk to strangers, ignore the strangers' problems so I could talk to them about videogames. Hmm... that reminds me of something, spending time with and about games and not confronting the inevitability of horror and mortality. *opens a news site to see today’s fresh hell* Hmm... *goes back to writing a review for a game* No, can't place why that would be so relatable.
